00722.title: TCHP: before surgery and beyond
00722.summary: Six cycles before surgery are one part of the pathway. Surgery findings determine the treatment afterwards; hormone treatment is added only if the cancer is also hormone-receptor positive.

lanes.label: Cancer medicines
cells: HER2 treatment chosen from pathology; commonly to complete a year overall

lanes.label: Surgery
cells: Review response and plan the operation
Lumpectomy OR mastectomy; lymph-node surgery as indicated
Report new breast, arm or scar concerns

lanes.label: Radiotherapy
cells: Discuss whether likely to be needed
Usually planned after chemotherapy and surgery
If indicated: may overlap HER2 treatment; team agrees timing
Review skin, fatigue and late effects

lanes.label: Endocrine / bone care
cells: Endocrine treatment if indicated; assess bone protection
Endocrine treatment can continue for years; DEXA by risk

lanes.label: Blood tests
cells: Blood count, kidney and liver tests; GFR
Preoperative checks arranged by surgical team

lanes.label: Heart checks
cells: Carry the cardiac monitoring plan forward
Continue HER2 surveillance; assessment at completion

lanes.label: Cancer imaging
cells: Clinical response review; imaging for concern or surgical planning
Annual mammography; no routine CT/markers if well

milestones.title: Heart ultrasound (echo)
milestones.when: Before HER2 therapy; every 12 weeks during it; at completion
milestones.why: Checks heart pumping function, even without symptoms.
milestones.action: Ask when the next echo is due and who arranges it. Report new breathlessness, swelling or palpitations.
milestones.clinical: NCCP baseline LVEF ≥55%; impaired function may need 4–8-week reassessment. After completion, ESC surveillance is risk-based; do not end cardiac follow-up merely because chemotherapy stops.

milestones.title: Response and operation planning
milestones.when: During neoadjuvant treatment and before surgery
milestones.why: Checks the local response and helps plan surgery.
milestones.action: Ask which breast imaging is planned and whether the result changes the operation.
milestones.clinical: Regular clinical examination. Use the most informative baseline modality for imaging follow-up; no universal CT at each cycle.

milestones.title: After surgery: choose the next pathway
milestones.when: When pathology is available
milestones.why: Residual cancer and receptor status can change the postoperative medicines.
milestones.action: Ask for the name, purpose and planned duration of the next treatment.
milestones.clinical: NCCP 00722 describes further trastuzumab to complete one year. Contemporary postoperative HER2 selection requires MDT review, including a separate residual-disease pathway. NCCP 00726 is metastatic maintenance and must not be used as an automatic adjuvant continuation.

milestones.title: Bone health, if endocrine therapy is prescribed
milestones.when: At the endocrine-treatment decision; then by risk
milestones.why: Assess fracture risk and whether a baseline DEXA bone-density scan is needed when starting an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression/treatment-induced menopause. It may already have been done before this regimen.
milestones.action: Ask whether a DEXA result is already available and whether bone protection is recommended.
milestones.clinical: Repeat DEXA is based on baseline bone density, fracture risk and bone treatment. A 12–24-month reassessment can be appropriate near a treatment threshold or when risk changes; it is not an automatic annual scan for everyone. NICE baseline DEXA criteria include the exception for patients already receiving adjuvant bisphosphonates.

milestones.title: Surveillance after early breast treatment
milestones.when: After completion of local treatment
milestones.why: Annual mammography of remaining breast tissue after treatment; the team sets the first date. The mastectomy side is not routinely mammographed. New symptoms need assessment between visits.
milestones.action: Report new symptoms without waiting for the next mammogram.
milestones.clinical: Routine CT, PET or tumour-marker blood tests are not recommended simply to look for recurrence after early breast treatment in someone without symptoms. Imaging is arranged for a clinical reason.

clinical_notes: Radiotherapy, endocrine therapy and HER2 continuation can overlap when the MDT considers this appropriate. The map does not prescribe exact postoperative start dates.
The echo interval runs from the HER2 treatment course; changing phase does not reset monitoring.

00857.title: Pembrolizumab and chemotherapy: the whole breast pathway
00857.setting: Neoadjuvant → surgery → adjuvant · triple-negative early breast cancer
00857.summary: This is NCCP 00857: four 3-week cycles of carboplatin/weekly paclitaxel with pembrolizumab, then four 3-week AC cycles with pembrolizumab, surgery, and postoperative pembrolizumab when appropriate.

lanes.label: Cancer medicines
cells: Pembrolizumab + carboplatin D1; paclitaxel D1/8/15 ×4 cycles
Pembrolizumab: 9 doses every 3 weeks OR 5 doses every 6 weeks
Immune effects can occur after the last dose

lanes.label: Surgery
cells: Image for surgical planning as needed
Lumpectomy OR mastectomy; lymph-node surgery as indicated

lanes.label: Radiotherapy
cells: Not part of these chemotherapy cycles
Decision based on surgery and pathology
If indicated: may overlap pembrolizumab under the agreed plan

lanes.label: Blood / immune checks
cells: Blood count, kidney/liver tests, glucose and thyroid tests
Bloods weekly in cycles 1–4; glucose each cycle
Bloods and glucose before each cycle
Bloods per pembrolizumab plan; thyroid every 3–6 weeks
Review unresolved or new immune symptoms

lanes.label: Heart checks
cells: Cardiac history / ECG; echo according to anthracycline risk
Doxorubicin exposure: additional monitoring by risk
Tell anaesthetic team about cardiac/immune problems
Cardiac assessment if symptoms or prior toxicity

lanes.label: Cancer imaging
cells: Annual mammography; no routine CT/markers if well

milestones.title: Know when the chemotherapy changes
milestones.when: After four 3-week cycles
milestones.why: The weekly paclitaxel visits stop and the AC phase starts.
milestones.action: Confirm which medicines and supportive medicines change.
milestones.clinical: This is q3-week AC 60/600. Do not substitute a dose-dense AC or pembrolizumab 400 mg neoadjuvant variant.

milestones.title: Thyroid and other immune checks
milestones.when: Thyroid tests every 3–6 weeks; glucose each cycle; other tests as indicated
milestones.why: Pembrolizumab can inflame hormone glands and other organs.
milestones.action: Report diarrhoea, breathlessness, severe fatigue, thirst, headache, rash or jaundice promptly.
milestones.clinical: NCCP: cortisol as indicated. Grade-specific immune toxicity is handled separately from cytotoxic dose changes. Pembrolizumab is withheld/stopped, not dose-reduced.

milestones.title: Heart assessment around doxorubicin
milestones.when: Before and during the anthracycline phase, according to risk
milestones.why: Doxorubicin can affect the heart; ECG and echo answer different questions.
milestones.action: Ask whether a baseline echo and follow-up cardiac tests are needed.
milestones.clinical: NCCP specifies baseline ECG and echo/MUGA when >65 or clinically indicated, with LVEF >50% for doxorubicin. ESC recommends broader baseline echocardiographic assessment for anthracyclines and risk-based follow-up. Agree the local cardiac pathway.

milestones.title: Postoperative medicines and radiotherapy
milestones.when: After pathology and recovery
milestones.why: The team combines recurrence-risk information, tolerance and the operation result.
milestones.action: Ask whether radiotherapy overlaps the remaining pembrolizumab and which clinician coordinates the plan.
milestones.clinical: Residual-disease or germline-BRCA-directed additions require separate indication review; this map does not automatically add capecitabine or olaparib.

milestones.title: Surveillance and lasting effects
milestones.when: After early breast treatment
milestones.why: Annual mammography of remaining breast tissue after treatment; the team sets the first date. The mastectomy side is not routinely mammographed. New symptoms need assessment between visits.
milestones.action: Report new symptoms early, including after immunotherapy has stopped.
milestones.clinical: Routine CT, PET or tumour-marker blood tests are not recommended simply to look for recurrence after early breast treatment in someone without symptoms. Imaging is arranged for a clinical reason. DEXA is not routinely required solely because of pembrolizumab; assess if treatment causes menopause or another bone-risk indication arises.

clinical_notes: TNBC does not have a routine adjuvant endocrine-therapy lane. Treatment-induced menopause still merits symptom and bone-health assessment.
The interval to surgery and radiation depends on recovery and the MDT plan. Columns show sequence, not equal lengths of time.

00619.title: Adjuvant abemaciclib: two years within a longer plan
00619.setting: Adjuvant · high-risk node-positive HR-positive / HER2-negative early breast cancer
00619.summary: Abemaciclib is taken with endocrine treatment after surgery and other indicated local/systemic treatment. Abemaciclib is planned for two years; endocrine treatment commonly continues beyond that.

lanes.label: Surgery / chemotherapy
cells: Lumpectomy OR mastectomy; chemotherapy if indicated
No routine additional chemotherapy in this regimen

lanes.label: Radiotherapy
cells: After surgery and chemotherapy when indicated
Confirm completion and start plan with team
Any overlap requires an explicit specialist plan

lanes.label: Abemaciclib
cells: Check medicines and provide diarrhoea plan
Continue without a planned week off
Stop at planned completion or earlier if needed

lanes.label: Endocrine treatment
cells: Confirm chosen drug; ovarian suppression if needed
Usually continues for years; review duration

lanes.label: Blood tests
cells: Blood count, kidney/liver and bone profile

lanes.label: Bone health
cells: Review fracture risk and prior DEXA
Repeat DEXA by risk, often considered at 12–24 months

lanes.label: Cancer / heart tests
cells: Record baseline cancer and cardiac history
No routine echo solely for abemaciclib
Tests for symptoms or prior-treatment risks
Annual mammography; no routine CT/markers if well

milestones.title: Early blood monitoring
milestones.when: Baseline; every 2 weeks for 2 months; monthly for the next 2 months
milestones.why: Checks blood counts and kidney/liver/bone-profile results.
milestones.action: Confirm blood-test appointments even though the medicine is taken at home.
milestones.clinical: After month 4: as clinically indicated, with additional tests for toxicity. Do not copy a ribociclib monitoring schedule.

milestones.title: Early diarrhoea support
milestones.when: From the first loose stool and throughout treatment
milestones.why: Diarrhoea can develop early and cause dehydration.
milestones.action: Use the prescribed rescue plan and contact the team; do not wait for the next review.
milestones.clinical: Grade 2 that has not resolved within 24 h, persistent/recurrent grade 2, grade 3–4 or hospitalisation require the source interruption pathway. Do not automatically hold all first grade 2 episodes without duration/context.

milestones.title: Bone density and fracture risk
milestones.when: At AI/OFS initiation and then by risk
milestones.why: Assess fracture risk and whether a baseline DEXA bone-density scan is needed when starting an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression/treatment-induced menopause. It may already have been done before this regimen.
milestones.action: Ask when bone health was last assessed and whether a repeat scan or bone medicine is needed.
milestones.clinical: Repeat DEXA is based on baseline bone density, fracture risk and bone treatment. A 12–24-month reassessment can be appropriate near a treatment threshold or when risk changes; it is not an automatic annual scan for everyone. Tamoxifen alone is not an automatic baseline DEXA indication. Adjuvant bisphosphonate eligibility is a separate decision.

milestones.title: Breast surveillance
milestones.when: After early breast treatment
milestones.why: Annual mammography of remaining breast tissue after treatment; the team sets the first date. The mastectomy side is not routinely mammographed. New symptoms need assessment between visits.
milestones.action: Report symptoms promptly; a normal scheduled mammogram does not explain every new symptom.
milestones.clinical: Routine CT, PET or tumour-marker blood tests are not recommended simply to look for recurrence after early breast treatment in someone without symptoms. Imaging is arranged for a clinical reason.

milestones.title: Two-year transition
milestones.when: At planned abemaciclib completion
milestones.why: The CDK4/6 drug ends while endocrine treatment may continue.
milestones.action: Ask for the continuing endocrine, bone-health and follow-up plan.
milestones.clinical: Do not infer that endocrine therapy ends when abemaciclib ends. Prior anthracycline/HER2 exposure may create a separate cardiac follow-up need.

milestones.title: Baseline ECG
milestones.when: Before starting, as clinically indicated
milestones.why: Cardiac symptoms, history or other medicines may make an ECG appropriate.
milestones.action: Ask whether a baseline ECG is needed for your situation.
milestones.clinical: NCCP 00619 v4a p2. No universal abemaciclib Day 14 ECG requirement; do not import the ribociclib schedule.

clinical_notes: Entry includes surgery completed, node-positive high-risk criteria and source timing limits. An Oncotype result does not replace these requirements.
The pre-abemaciclib radiation sequence must be agreed explicitly; the NCCP drug schedule does not prescribe an automatic concurrent radiation course.

00726.title: HER2 maintenance: treatment and checks continue
00726.setting: Maintenance · HER2-positive metastatic / unresectable recurrent breast cancer
00726.summary: Pertuzumab and trastuzumab continue after the chemotherapy part of the metastatic treatment plan. Maintenance remains active treatment, with response and heart checks.

lanes.label: Cancer medicines
cells: Review benefit, tolerance and last dose date
Continue while benefit and tolerance support the plan
Ongoing treatment; no fixed one-year stopping rule

lanes.label: Local / endocrine care
cells: Endocrine therapy may be considered if HR-positive

lanes.label: Blood tests
cells: Blood count, kidney and liver tests
Continue according to the active regimen

lanes.label: Heart ultrasound
cells: Check latest echo and due interval
12-weekly default; interval changes require cardiac risk review

lanes.label: Cancer scans
cells: Usually every 2–4 months; modality / interval individualised

lanes.label: Tumour markers
cells: Confirm whether used for this person
Adjunct to symptoms and scans, never alone

milestones.title: Heart ultrasound
milestones.when: NCCP: baseline and every 12 weeks during HER2 treatment
milestones.why: Checks heart function while treatment continues.
milestones.action: Ask when the next echo is due; a move to maintenance does not restart the clock.
milestones.clinical: NCCP baseline LVEF ≥50%; 4–8-week checks may be needed with impairment. ESC allows consideration of 6-monthly TTE after the first year in selected asymptomatic low/moderate-risk metastatic patients with normal assessments. This does not automatically override the NCCP 12-week schedule; document the agreed specialist/local plan.

milestones.title: Response imaging
milestones.when: Usually every 2–4 months; earlier if clinically needed
milestones.why: A baseline scan records where the cancer is. Response is usually reviewed every 2–4 months, adjusted for the treatment, disease pace, symptoms and previous results. CT chest/abdomen/pelvis is common when appropriate; the team chooses the imaging needed for the known sites.
milestones.action: Ask what scan is planned, when results will be discussed and who to contact for new symptoms.
milestones.clinical: Choose consistent imaging of disease sites. Brain MRI or other additional imaging is indication-specific, not a universal recurring item.

milestones.title: Tumour markers, if useful
milestones.when: Only if included in the individual monitoring plan
milestones.why: CA 15-3 or CEA may be helpful in selected metastatic cases, especially if previously raised. They support the assessment with symptoms and imaging; a marker alone does not decide whether treatment is working or should change.
milestones.action: Ask what a change means alongside the scan and clinical review.

milestones.title: Missed or delayed infusion
milestones.when: Whenever a treatment gap occurs
milestones.why: A long gap can change the required antibody loading doses.
milestones.action: Contact the team to confirm the new prescription; do not assume the old visit plan still applies.
milestones.clinical: NCCP gap ≥6 weeks requires reloading of both antibodies. No routine percentage dose reduction for these antibodies.

milestones.title: Separate early-breast pathways
milestones.when: At every transition
milestones.why: This particular NCCP code is for metastatic/unresectable recurrent maintenance.
milestones.action: Ask the team to confirm the setting and aim on the written plan.
milestones.clinical: Do not label adjuvant trastuzumab/pertuzumab after TCHP as NCCP 00726. Use the relevant early-breast protocol.

clinical_notes: The map cannot label an echo or scan as ordered, booked, completed or overdue. It provides the expected plan for a clinical conversation.
A DEXA scan is considered for endocrine/menopause/fracture indications, not automatically because HER2 antibodies continue.

00525.title: Ribociclib: tablets, early checks and response reviews
00525.setting: Advanced / metastatic · HR-positive / HER2-negative breast cancer
00525.summary: Ribociclib is taken for three weeks of each four-week cycle with endocrine treatment. The first two cycles need extra blood checks and an early ECG; cancer-response reviews continue over the longer term.

lanes.label: Ribociclib
cells: Repeat 21 days on / 7 off if cleared
Repeat the same cycle unless changed
Continue while benefit and tolerance support it

lanes.label: Endocrine treatment
cells: Choose AI OR fulvestrant; ovarian suppression if needed
AI daily throughout OR fulvestrant loading visits
AI continues during ribociclib week off; injections as planned

lanes.label: ECG / electrolytes
cells: ECG; correct low potassium, magnesium, calcium or phosphate
ECG around Day 14; electrolytes before cycle
Electrolytes before cycle; ECG if indicated
Electrolytes before each cycle through cycle 6

lanes.label: Bone / local care
cells: DEXA or bone medicine if indicated
Radiation only under a separate local-treatment plan

milestones.title: ECG: an electrical heart tracing
milestones.when: Before starting and around Day 14 of cycle 1; then as indicated
milestones.why: Ribociclib can alter the QT interval, which affects heart rhythm.
milestones.action: Attend the early ECG and report fainting, palpitations or new dizziness promptly.
milestones.clinical: Starting QTcF must be <450 ms. This is ECG monitoring, not a routine 3-monthly echo programme. Review QT-prolonging/CYP3A medicines and electrolyte abnormalities.

milestones.title: Bloods and electrolytes
milestones.when: Bloods every 2 weeks for cycles 1–2; before cycles 3–6; then as indicated
milestones.why: Checks blood counts, kidney/liver tests and minerals relevant to heart rhythm.
milestones.action: Ask who checks the results before the next pack starts.
milestones.clinical: Electrolytes before each of the first six cycles, then as indicated; intensify monitoring with abnormal results.

milestones.title: Cancer-response imaging
milestones.when: Usually every 2–4 months, adapted to the clinical picture
milestones.why: A baseline scan records where the cancer is. Response is usually reviewed every 2–4 months, adjusted for the treatment, disease pace, symptoms and previous results. CT chest/abdomen/pelvis is common when appropriate; the team chooses the imaging needed for the known sites.
milestones.action: Ask how scan results, symptoms and your priorities will guide the next decision.

milestones.title: Markers, if selected
milestones.when: Alongside the individual response plan
milestones.why: CA 15-3 or CEA may be helpful in selected metastatic cases, especially if previously raised. They support the assessment with symptoms and imaging; a marker alone does not decide whether treatment is working or should change.
milestones.action: Ask whether markers add useful information in your case.

milestones.title: Bone health with endocrine therapy
milestones.when: At AI/OFS initiation and then by risk
milestones.why: Assess fracture risk and whether a baseline DEXA bone-density scan is needed when starting an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression/treatment-induced menopause. It may already have been done before this regimen.
milestones.action: Ask about DEXA, weight-bearing activity and any indicated bone treatment.
milestones.clinical: Repeat DEXA is based on baseline bone density, fracture risk and bone treatment. A 12–24-month reassessment can be appropriate near a treatment threshold or when risk changes; it is not an automatic annual scan for everyone.

milestones.title: Week off ribociclib
milestones.when: Days 22–28 of each cycle
milestones.why: The planned break applies to ribociclib, not automatically to the endocrine partner.
milestones.action: Follow the written prescription for each medicine; do not make up missed or vomited doses.
milestones.clinical: This metastatic schedule starts at 600 mg/day unless adjusted. Do not substitute the separate 400 mg/3-year adjuvant ribociclib pathway.

milestones.title: Optional pre-cycle review window
milestones.when: Local Day 25–26 if adopted
milestones.why: Allows time for results before the planned next cycle.
milestones.action: Restart only after the team confirms the result and prescription.
milestones.clinical: Operational convention; retain protocol early blood tests and ECG schedule. Endocrine treatment follows its own schedule.

clinical_notes: NCCP v6 and the current manufacturer QT table differ on restart after the first >480–500 ms event in metastatic disease. Interrupt and reconcile with pharmacy/cardiology before restart; no automatic restart dose is inferred.
NCCP eligibility wording is narrower on page 2 than its indications on page 1. Resolve the intended setting, endocrine partner and ovarian-suppression requirements.

00485.setting: Neoadjuvant or adjuvant · early breast cancer
00485.summary: Four AC treatments 14 days apart, followed 14 days after the last AC by 12 weekly paclitaxel doses, subject to recovery and review.

lanes.label: Cancer medicines
cells: AC every 14 days ×4; G-CSF each cycle
Endocrine or HER2 treatment only if separately indicated

lanes.label: Radiotherapy
cells: After surgery and recovery if indicated

lanes.label: Heart checks
cells: Symptoms or risk determine extra checks

lanes.label: Cancer imaging
cells: Image for surgery planning when indicated
Annual mammography of remaining breast tissue

milestones.title: Blood tests and treatment review
milestones.when: FBC, kidney/liver tests → Before each AC treatment → Before each weekly dose → Confirm recovery for surgery / RT → Tests according to ongoing medicines
milestones.why: Results may change whether a dose is given or held.
milestones.action: Confirm the booking and who reviews the result before treatment.

milestones.title: Heart tests
milestones.when: Baseline ECG; echo / LVEF assessment → Doxorubicin exposure and risk review → Symptoms or risk determine extra checks → Communicate prior anthracycline exposure → Risk-based post-treatment review

milestones.title: Imaging and markers

milestones.why: The purpose and frequency depend on early versus advanced disease.

milestones.title: Bone health with endocrine treatment
milestones.when: At endocrine / ovarian-suppression planning; repeat by risk
milestones.why: Low oestrogen can affect bone strength.
milestones.action: Ask whether DEXA, fracture-risk assessment or bone protection is appropriate.
milestones.clinical: NICE baseline DEXA criteria exclude those already receiving adjuvant bisphosphonates. Repeat intervals are individualised; reassessment in 12–24 months may be appropriate near a treatment threshold.

milestones.title: Who arranges and reviews each check?
milestones.when: At initiation and every handover
milestones.why: A recommended test can be missed if responsibility is unclear.
milestones.action: Ask the team to document the booking owner, result reviewer, due window and escalation route.

clinical_notes: No trastuzumab phase is automatically part of NCCP 00485. HER2-directed treatment needs its own indication and cardiac plan.
